newsitem.title: USA: LPC - Syndicated loan market wrap-up November 18-22.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Syndicated loan market wrap-up November 18-22.

text.p: NEW YORK, Nov 22 (LPC) - U.S. syndicated loan volume rebounded significantly this week, with more than $8.8 billion in new loans introduced to the market, according to bankers and loan traders.
The jump in volume comes after a week of just $4 billion in loans introduced to market, bankers said.
For the second straight week, new issues of higher-yielding, leveraged loans cracked the $1 billion mark, racking up $1.5 billion in volume, sources said.
Most notable in the leveraged market is a $450 million deal for Berkline Holding, according to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing.
There are now roughly $11.2 billion in leveraged loans available in the syndications market, according to lenders and traders.
Investment-grade deals brought to market this week totaled $7.3 billion, a big gain from last week's $3.1 billion, according to market sources.
High-profile, creditworthy borrowers continue to take advantage of favorable lending conditions, returning to market to refinance at lower spreads and fees, sources said.
Returning to the market this week were Rockwell International Corp and TCI Communications Inc, bankers added.
The Rockwell credit, arranged by J.P. Morgan, is structured as a $1.5 billion, five-year revolver and a $500 million 364-day facility, sources said.
It will refinance a loan from December 1994 which the company used to back its acquisition of Reliance Electric, sources added.
There are now roughly $55 billion in investment-grade credits either launched or being prepared for syndication, market sources said.
Overall loan volume now available in the U.S. syndicated loan market stands at $66.2 billion, according to lenders and traders. - Nelson Arce, LPC Editorial, 212 489-5455
